newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Court restores opposition victory in Serbian town.
newsitem.headline: Court restores opposition victory in Serbian town.

text.p: A court in the southern town of Nis ordered the city election commission to hand back victory won in November 17 elections to the opposition, an official of Serbia's opposition Zajedno (Together) coalition said on Sunday.
"We have been informed by the court that it has ordered the city commission to acknowledge our election victory within 10 days," the Zajedno spokeswoman said.
Officials were not immediately available to confirm her statement.
Zajedno says it was cheated of victory in local elections in November in major towns including the capital Belgrade and the industrial town of Nis.
It said Nis's city election commission forged results in 17 election districts handing victory to the ruling socialists.
The alleged election fraud has prompted Zajedno and students to demonstrate on the streets of Belgrade and other big towns in Serbia for the past 28 days.
The Nis district court ordered the election commission last week to hand over all election documents.
